retrieval_timing_is_budgeting.name: retrieval_timing_is_budgeting

predictions.depends_on: the run oracle-decision cell (static where the static re-run succeeded, retrieval at start elsewhere) against the always-retrieve re-run, with the value 'read off the 2x2 paired (static success, retrieval success) contingency table'
predictions.falsifier: the oracle exceeds always-retrieve by 8 net or more, i.e. retrieval fails on at least 8 percent of the episodes the static prompt solves
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: the estimand is stated two incompatible ways and neither gives a clean test: the table version P(static succeeds and retrieval fails) is an algebraic function of the same two measured cells it is compared with and is non-negative by construction while being inflated by per-episode test-retest flips, and the run version subtracts a regression-to-the-mean loss taken on exactly the episodes selected for having succeeded once, so the confirming 'within +/-8' outcome is produced by the arm's design rather than by the bound being small.
predictions.fix: pre-register a single estimand - the table-computed discordance mass with its McNemar CI - and calibrate it against a static-vs-static discordance null from the test-retest re-run, so the bound is separated from the test-retest loss the run oracle inherits.

predictions.depends_on: the threshold-2 goal-key expert-pool stall cell plus its firing log, against the always-retrieve re-run, with the fixed-step (step 10) schedule cell as the second test
predictions.falsifier: stall is below always-retrieve by more than 8 net, or fires on more than 50 percent of episodes, or the schedule falls below the stall trigger by more than 8 net
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: firing rate and late-retrieval loss are both free empirical quantities that can break the prediction, though the net falsifier is one-sided: a stall arm beating always-retrieve by more than 8 net would directly contradict 'timing is only budgeting' and is not listed as falsifying, and the firing-rate clause can falsify for a reason about the detector rather than about timing value.

predictions.depends_on: the planted-recovery failure-key stall cell (100 percent coverage of five failure modes, ~40-token items keyed by failure text) against the expert-pool goal-key stall cell
predictions.falsifier: the difference is below +8 net
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: the reader can fail to apply a short recovery hint delivered mid-episode, so this positive control can genuinely fail, although the contrast changes the key and the bank at once and therefore cannot attribute a pass to the failure key rather than to the planted content.

predictions.depends_on: the self-pool failure-key stall cell against the expert goal-key stall cell and the random-at-stall cell, where the self pool is the agent's own detour windows with unmeasured recovery coverage
predictions.falsifier: self-pool failure-key retrieval exceeds either reference by more than 8 net
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: the predicted null re-describes how the self pool was built - its coverage of the five failure modes is never measured, unlike the planted bank's stated 100 percent - so a null cannot separate 'the natural pool is decorative for the failure key' from 'there was no recovery in the pool to retrieve'.
predictions.fix: measure and report the self pool's recovery coverage rate (as the binding proposal measures p_nat for its natural level) and add a coverage-matched self-pool subsample, so the arm tests the key at a known content availability.

predictions.depends_on: the rulebook static cell and the rulebook+planted-stall-retrieval cell against the planted failure-key stall cell; the rulebook is the same five planted items concatenated into the cached prefix
predictions.falsifier: planted retrieval beats the rulebook by 8 net or more, or rulebook+retrieval beats rulebook alone by 8 net or more
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: content is identical by construction so neither falsifier can fire through information, only through delivery position at the moment of failure, but the rulebook+retrieval arm does vary position with content held fixed, which makes that channel instrumented rather than unnamed.

shared_terms: P1-P2: both are net differences from the same always-retrieve re-run cell, so that cell's test-retest noise shifts both in the same direction.

P1 internal: oracle minus always-retrieve is a function of the static re-run and always-retrieve outcomes (the paired 2x2 table), so the oracle cell is not an independent measurement of the quantity it reports.
P3-P4: both are scored against the same expert-pool goal-key stall cell, so that cell's level simultaneously sets the size of P3's gain and the width of P4's null.
P3-P5: P5's reference is the planted failure-key stall cell that P3 defines, so a null P3 turns P5's equivalence into a match between two nulls (the proposal notes this only for P4).

rank_flat_retriever_is_a_type_classifier.name: rank_flat_retriever_is_a_type_classifier

predictions.depends_on: the within-type rank 50-52 cell against the rank 1-3 (Measurement A) re-run, items length-matched inside each rank window, deepest available window declared for types with fewer than 55 items
predictions.falsifier: rank 1-3 exceeds rank 50-52 by more than 8 net
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: deep-rank items lose object and receptacle match - a change the design itself measures via same-object and same-receptacle recall - so a real drop is reachable, and the fallback to the deepest available window only weakens the manipulation on a declared subset of thin types.

predictions.depends_on: the L1 (type, object class id, target receptacle id) and L2 (type, object class id) leave-out cells against the full-bank top-3 cell
predictions.falsifier: either L1 or L2 drops success by 8 net or more
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: the falsifier is reachable if object-matched neighbours carry the gain, but L2's retrieval from the remainder is the within-type rank ladder under another name, so P1's flatness would already force P2's null rather than P2 testing it independently.

predictions.depends_on: the L3 cell (all same-type items removed, then top-3 from the remainder) against the re-run random wrong-type fixed-exemplar placebo from Measurement C
predictions.falsifier: L3 stays more than 8 net above the placebo
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: top-3 retrieval from a type-stripped bank is exactly the most-similar-wrong-type construction of P4, which the proposal predicts sits more than 8 net below the random wrong-type placebo, so under the proposal's own mechanism the one-sided falsifier cannot fire and the null is protected from below by the very harm P4 asserts.
predictions.fix: make the falsifier two-sided and add a random-wrong-type retrieved cell matched to the placebo's selection rule and item count, so L3 is compared with a like-for-like reference instead of a fixed single exemplar.

predictions.depends_on: the most-similar wrong-type retrieval cell (the 'Examples' header cell, nearest other-type neighbours by bge-m3 to the goal) against Measurement C's re-run random wrong-type fixed exemplar
predictions.falsifier: the gap is smaller than 8 net
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: compliance need not scale with similarity and the gap can plausibly come out under 8 net, although the contrast varies delivery (three retrieved items vs one fixed exemplar, with no stated token matching for the placebo) alongside similarity, so a pass would not isolate similarity.

predictions.depends_on: the 'Retrieved from memory', 'Instructions' and mismatch-warning framing cells, all carrying the same most-similar wrong-type items, against the 'Examples' cell
predictions.falsifier: either neutral header shifts success by 8 net or more, or the mismatch warning fails to raise success by 8 net
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: header effects on compliance are free to be large in either direction and the warning positive control can genuinely fail; the only structural risk is downside compression if P4's predicted harm leaves the 'Examples' cell near a floor, which the design does not bound in advance.

predictions.depends_on: the per-type cached sub-bank cell (up to 80 items, ~11k tokens, one cached prefix per type) against rank 1-3, plus logged uncached prefill per episode
predictions.falsifier: the sub-bank is below rank 1-3 by more than 8 net
predictions.label: open
predictions.reason: many-shot dilution at ~11k tokens is a real failure route for the success clause even though the sub-bank contains the top-3 items, but the conjunction's cost clause is true by construction - a cached per-type prefix has lower uncached prefill than per-episode retrieval regardless of outcome - so only half the prediction is testable.

predictions.depends_on: the type-agnostic top-3 cell retrieved over the whole bank against the type-conditioned top-3 cell, with type read from the goal sentence
predictions.falsifier: the type-agnostic cell is below the type-conditioned cell by more than 8 net
predictions.label: near_entailed
predictions.reason: falsification requires whole-bank goal-keyed similarity to return wrong-type items at a material rate, which ALFWorld's templated and type-diagnostic goal sentences make close to impossible, and the wrong-type return rate is not among the reported secondary metrics, so the null is fixed by the encoder rather than tested by the arm.
predictions.fix: report the type-agnostic arm's wrong-type return rate as a gating manipulation check and add a degraded-key variant (type verb masked, or an object-only key) so a nonzero wrong-type rate exists for the prediction to be about.

shared_terms: P1-P2: both are differences from the same rank 1-3 re-run cell, and L2's retrieval from the remainder is the within-type rank ladder by another name, so P1's flatness determines P2's null.

P3-P4: the L3 cell and the most-similar wrong-type harm cell are the same construction (top-3 by similarity among other-type items), so P4's predicted harm fixes where L3 sits relative to the random wrong-type placebo.
P4-P5: every framing cell is the similar-wrong arm with a different header, so P4's harm level is the baseline all P5 contrasts are measured from and a large P4 harm compresses P5's downside.
P1-P6: the sub-bank contains the rank 1-3 items, so P6's success clause is P1's flatness plus a context-dilution term measured against the same rank 1-3 cell.
P4-P7: P7 can only fail through the wrong-type items P4 uses as its harm channel, so the two predictions rest on the same unreported quantity - the retriever's wrong-type return rate.
rank_flat_retriever_is_a_type_classifier.headline: P1
